schema:
CREATE TABLE event_types (
    event_type_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name        TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- what identifies the type (e.g. user_message)
    created_at  TEXT    NOT NULL    -- UTC time the type was defined
)

CREATE TABLE events (
    row_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,  -- insertion order; what `read` sorts by. Not
                                      -- AUTOINCREMENT: that spends an id (and a
                                      -- write) on every duplicate DO NOTHING
                                      -- skips. Rows are never deleted, so ids
                                      -- are never reused either way.
    inserted_at TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- UTC time the event was first stored
    event_id    TEXT,               -- the caller's id for the event: what makes a
                                    -- re-sent event a duplicate. NULL = the caller
                                    -- gave none; the row is then its own event,
                                    -- known by row_id, and never a duplicate.
    event_type_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES event_types (event_type_id),
    payload_json TEXT   NOT NULL,   -- the payload, as given
    tokens      INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- the caller's count if it gave one, else the
                                    -- tokenizer's count of `text` (of payload_json
                                    -- without one), taken at insert
    text        TEXT,               -- the event's readable text, as the caller gave it:
                                    -- what a policy shows and counts of it. NULL: none
    counted     INTEGER             -- 1: `tokens` is the model's provider's count, set after
                                    -- insert (`record_counts`); NULL: the caller's or the tokenizer's
                                    -- given; its payload as JSON stands in
                                    -- (then a p_<name> column per property: add_properties)
, p_channel, p_cwd, p_poller, p_kind, p_words, p_read_id, p_answer_id)

CREATE TABLE event_type_properties (
    event_type_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES event_types (event_type_id),
    name        TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- the property; its column is p_<name>
    required    INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- 1: an event of the type must carry it
    identifies  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- 1: part of an event's identity, with its id
    PRIMARY KEY (event_type_id, name)
)

CREATE TABLE _made_items (
    made_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at  TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- (and the properties of the read it was made for)
    name        TEXT,               -- what it is, in the manager's terms
    source      TEXT,               -- what made it, in the manager's terms (e.g. a build)
    item_json   TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- the item, exactly as returned by read
    tokens      INTEGER,            -- its size, by the manager's tokenizer (or, `counted`, the provider's)
    counted     INTEGER,            -- 1: `tokens` is the provider's count (`record_counts`)
    sha         TEXT                -- of its name, source and text (`made_sha`): what makes it the same item;
                                    -- NULL: made by an older ag, not yet folded (migrate.py)
, p_channel, p_cwd, p_poller, p_kind, p_words, p_read_id, p_answer_id)

CREATE TABLE _reads (
    read_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    read_at     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- (and the read's properties)
    row_id      INTEGER,            -- the event (an events row) the read responded to
    manager     TEXT,               -- which implementation read
    basis       TEXT,               -- what the context was built from, in the
                                    -- manager's terms (e.g. a build id); NULL = none
    est_tokens  INTEGER,            -- the context's size by the manager's own count; NULL = not given
    real_tokens INTEGER,            -- its size as the model's provider counted it (the
                                    -- call's input tokens, reported after it); NULL = not yet
    limit_tokens INTEGER,           -- the harness's own limit the call stated (where it compacts,
                                    -- or its window ends); NULL = none
    preamble_json TEXT,             -- the harness's preamble the call stated: the _preambles it
                                    -- sent besides its messages, as a JSON list of ids; NULL = none
    sent_tokens INTEGER,            -- all the call sent -- every item and the preamble -- as the
                                    -- manager counted it at the read (less what the harness then
                                    -- left out, as it reports); NULL = not known
    pid         INTEGER,            -- the harness's process that made the call, and when it started
    pid_started TEXT,               -- ("<boot id>:<start ticks>", so a reused pid is not it); NULL = not known
    run         TEXT,               -- the harness's run that made the call, as its launcher named it (the hook
                                    -- server's /r/<run>/: codex's, the id of the process ag started); NULL = none
    error_status INTEGER,           -- no longer set: a failed call is a `call_failed` event (an older
    error       TEXT,               -- file's copied there once, `_migrated`)
    answered_at TEXT,               -- no longer set: an answer is its `reply_end` event
    context_id  INTEGER             -- the reads it shares its context with: those with the same properties
                                    -- (set as it is logged, `_reads_context`); NULL: an older file's, until moved
, p_channel, p_cwd, p_poller, p_kind, p_words, p_read_id, p_answer_id)

CREATE TABLE _contexts (
    context_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    key         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE   -- the properties set, as JSON, by name (`context_key`)
)

CREATE TABLE _preambles (
    preamble_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name        TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- what it is, as the harness names it: "instructions", "tools", ...
    sha         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- of the name and the text
    text        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    tokens      INTEGER,            -- its size, by the manager's tokenizer (or, `counted`, the provider's)
    counted     INTEGER             -- 1: `tokens` is the provider's count (`record_counts`)
)

CREATE TABLE _read_items (
    read_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    position    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    row_id      INTEGER,
    made_id     INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (read_id, position),
    CHECK ((row_id IS NULL) != (made_id IS NULL))
)

CREATE TABLE _stays (
    context_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    position    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    row_id      INTEGER,
    made_id     INTEGER,
    from_read   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    to_read     INTEGER,
    CHECK ((row_id IS NULL) != (made_id IS NULL))
)

CREATE TABLE _made_folded (
    old         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    made_id     INTEGER NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID

CREATE TABLE _polls (
    name        TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,    -- the poller's name
    polled_at   REAL    NOT NULL        -- seconds since the epoch
)

CREATE TABLE _withdrawn (
    row_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,  -- the event (an events row)
    withdrawn_at TEXT    NOT NULL,     -- when (UTC, ISO)
    read_id      INTEGER               -- the read of the call it came with; NULL = not known
)

CREATE TABLE _open (
    session     TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,   -- the session: its calls' `channel`
    pid         INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- the harness's process, and when it started
    pid_started TEXT    NOT NULL,      -- ("<boot id>:<start ticks>", as _reads has it)
    opened_at   TEXT    NOT NULL,
    opened_by   TEXT,                  -- what claimed it: "launcher", "call"
    yields      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0   -- 1: idle, and gives way to another process's claim
)

CREATE TABLE _migrated (
    name        TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,
    at          TEXT    NOT NULL
)

CREATE TABLE tasks (
    channel_key    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    task_index     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    name           TEXT    NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT,
    first_row      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_row       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    tokens         INTEGER,
    retention_json TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (channel_key, task_index)
)

CREATE TABLE cleaned_messages (
    row_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    text        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    build_id    INTEGER                  -- the build whose summary wrote it
)

CREATE TABLE _builds (
    build_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    channel_key       TEXT NOT NULL,
    status            TEXT NOT NULL,     -- running / ready / failed / nothing
    started_at        REAL NOT NULL,
    finished_at       REAL,
    through_row       INTEGER,           -- the last row the analysis saw
    open_from_row     INTEGER,           -- where the running (open) task starts
    ranking_json      TEXT,              -- earlier tasks, most relevant first: [[channel_key, task_index], ...]
    parallel_mark     INTEGER,           -- other channels' rows up to here were seen
    error             TEXT,
    reason            TEXT               -- why it was started: limit / boundary / request / direct
)

CREATE TABLE _boundaries (
    row_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,     -- the user message (an events row)
    channel_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    asked_at    REAL NOT NULL,
    decided_at  REAL,
    new_task    INTEGER,                 -- 1 / 0; NULL = not decided yet
    why         TEXT
)
CREATE INDEX events_type ON events (event_type_id)
CREATE INDEX _stays_open ON _stays (context_id, position) WHERE to_read IS NULL
CREATE INDEX _stays_from ON _stays (context_id, from_read)
CREATE INDEX _reads_context ON _reads (context_id, read_id)
CREATE INDEX _read_items_row ON _read_items (row_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX _made_items_sha ON _made_items (sha)
CREATE INDEX _builds_channel ON _builds (channel_key, build_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX events_id ON events (ifnull(p_channel, ''), event_id)

CREATE INDEX _reads_properties ON _reads (ifnull(p_channel, ''), ifnull(p_cwd, ''), ifnull(p_poller, ''), ifnull(p_kind, ''), ifnull(p_words, ''), ifnull(p_read_id, ''), ifnull(p_answer_id, ''), read_id)

CREATE TRIGGER _reads_context AFTER INSERT ON _reads WHEN NEW.context_id IS NULL BEGIN INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _contexts (key) VALUES (json_patch('{}', json_object('answer_id', NEW.p_answer_id, 'channel', NEW.p_channel, 'cwd', NEW.p_cwd, 'kind', NEW.p_kind, 'poller', NEW.p_poller, 'read_id', NEW.p_read_id, 'words', NEW.p_words))); UPDATE _reads SET context_id = (SELECT context_id FROM _contexts WHERE key = json_patch('{}', json_object('answer_id', NEW.p_answer_id, 'channel', NEW.p_channel, 'cwd', NEW.p_cwd, 'kind', NEW.p_kind, 'poller', NEW.p_poller, 'read_id', NEW.p_read_id, 'words', NEW.p_words))) WHERE read_id = NEW.read_id; END

replies.text:
At the edge of Bellweather Point stood a lighthouse painted white, though salt and storms had worn it the color of old bone. Every evening, Mara climbed its spiral stairs and lit the great lamp. Every morning, she counted the ships that had found their way home.

Her father had kept the light before her. He used to say the sea was a dark road and the lighthouse its promise: someone was watching.

One November night, fog swallowed the coast. The lamp’s turning beam vanished a few feet from the tower, and the wind shoved rain against the windows. Mara heard the harbor bell ring once, then twice. A boat was out there, lost.

She climbed to the lantern room and found the lamp sputtering. Its oil line had frozen. Below, in the keeper’s cupboard, lay her father’s brass hand lantern, dented from years of use. Mara lit it, wrapped her coat around the flame, and carried it to the narrow balcony.

The storm snatched at her sleeves. She raised the lantern high and swept it from side to side. For a long while, nothing answered. Then, through the fog, came a faint flash: a boat’s signal.

Mara kept moving the lantern. The answering flash grew nearer, disappeared, then returned. At last the fishing boat’s bow emerged beneath the cliff, guided toward the harbor mouth. Men on deck waved as they passed the rocks.

By dawn, the lamp was burning again. The fishermen brought Mara a loaf of warm bread and a small silver bell salvaged from their boat. They hung it beside the lighthouse door, where it chimed whenever the wind turned east.

Years later, when Mara’s own hands had grown unsteady, a child came to learn the keeper’s work. Before teaching her the lamp, Mara showed her the little bell.

“Listen,” she said. “The sea tells us when someone needs a light.”

That evening, the child climbed the stairs alone. Far below, the harbor bell rang once, then twice. She turned the lamp toward the dark, and the old lighthouse answered.
